q1: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ITM.ITEMNO, ITEMPRICE.NP FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
counterexample: INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMNO, NP) VALUES (1, 10), (1, 20), (2, 30); INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMNO, TYPE) VALUES (1, 1), (2, 2);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses a subquery to first select distinct ITEMNO and NP from the ITP table, and then joins this result with the ITM table. Q2, on the other hand, directly joins the ITP and ITM tables on ITEMNO without any subquery or distinct selection.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when the ITP table contains duplicate ITEMNO values with different NP values, and the ITM table contains the same ITEMNO values. In this case, Q1 will return each ITEMNO only once with the NP value from the first occurrence in the ITP table, while Q2 will return each ITEMNO with all its corresponding NP values from the ITP table.

q2_validation_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITM.ITEMNO, ITP.NP FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
